standard.title: Representations in literary texts reflect context
standard.description: analyse representations of individuals, groups and places and evaluate how they reflect their context in literary texts by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors
standard.prior_knowledge: Students analyse how people and places are represented in literary texts across historical, social and cultural contexts (AC9E9LE01). They have not yet evaluated how representations reflect the specific context in which they were produced.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse representations of individuals, groups and places and evaluate how they reflect their context in literary texts by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors.

nodes.label: Analysing representations of individuals and groups
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how individuals and groups are represented in a literary text, identifying specific textual choices that construct those representations.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse how at least one individual or group is represented in a provided literary text, identifying specific language and structural choices that construct the representation.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how individuals, groups and places are represented across a literary text, examining a range of textual choices and explaining how each contributes to the representation.
wider: Analyse representations of the same group (e.g. the underdog, the outsider) across multiple literary texts from different authors, comparing how the representation differs
Examine representations of First Nations Australians in texts by non-First Nations Australian authors and compare with representations in texts by First Nations Australian authors
Analyse how representations of places in literary texts construct cultural or national identity
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to evaluate representations as reflections of context — a judgement that is only coherent if students can first identify and analyse what the representation is. Thin treatment here leaves Node 2 without the analytical foundation it depends on.

response_modes.reason: Students often assume that a text's representation is neutral or obvious; encountering contrasting representations of the same group from different author positions resolves this and builds critical reading of representation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Representation analysis is rich across First Nations, Australian and world literary texts — comparative work across author positions (insider/outsider) and cultural contexts offers substantial analytic depth.
success_criteria: Identifies specific textual choices that construct the representation of at least one individual or group
Analyses how those textual choices contribute to the representation

nodes.label: Evaluating representations as reflections of context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how the representations in a literary text reflect the context in which it was produced, making a supported judgement.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate how at least one representation in a literary text reflects the social, cultural or historical context of its production, with supporting evidence.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate how representations across a literary text reflect the context in which it was written — including social, cultural and historical context — making reasoned judgements with textual evidence.
wider: Evaluate how texts that retell or adapt traditional stories (e.g. the anti-hero, the underdog) reflect their contemporary context differently from the original
Evaluate how First Nations Australian authors contemporise or modernise traditional stories, examining what choices reflect contemporary context and what choices maintain tradition
Compare how the same event or social issue is represented in literary texts from different time periods and evaluate what each reflection reveals about its context

response_modes.reason: Evaluating a representation as a reflection of context requires students to hold both the text and the context in mind simultaneously and reason about the relationship — this inference structure needs explicit teaching.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Evaluation of how representation reflects context is the core critical literacy skill — First Nations Australian texts and world literature from diverse contexts offer rich material for sustained evaluative work.
success_criteria: Identifies the context relevant to a representation in a literary text
Makes a supported judgement about how the representation reflects that context, with textual evidence
